evaluations.label: A
errors: Project code 'TS3012a' is never mentioned in the transcript
Project Manager called 'Markoff'; transcript says 'Mark'
Names misspelled: 'Dirk Mangfelt' (Meinfeld), 'Savier Jokins' (Xavier Juergens)
UI designer labeled 'Speaker 4' although he introduced himself as Nick Broer
'Speaker 4 clarifies that the scope of the project is limited to a TV remote control': the UI designer asked; the Project Manager clarified
Lists 'multi-remote or TV only' as an open question, yet the transcript (and A's own outline) shows it was settled as TV only
'lightweight materials that are aesthetically impactful': 'aesthetically impactful' is not in the transcript
Action items with no owners and generic content not assigned in the meeting
strengths: Covers the brief, three-phase process, price targets, roles and the animal exercise
Mentions the 30-minute reconvene and personal assignments
weaknesses: Several invented or wrong names and an invented project code
Internal contradiction about the multi-remote scope
Action items are unowned and not really stated in the meeting; omits that the personal coach gives assignments

evaluations.label: B
errors: 'urged familiarity and rational changes': the transcript says 'No rational changes... revolutionary changes', meaning is garbled and B's reading is doubtful
Action item owner spelled 'Dirk Mengveld' (transcript: Dirk Meinfeld)
'They set a €25 selling price': the price was given by the Project Manager as a brief, not set by the team (minor)
Some timestamps are off (e.g. project folder tagged [01:08], said at ~03:23)
strengths: Correct names for Mark, Dirk and Xavier and correct attribution of who said what
Accurately notes that the personal coach gives assignments and the team meets again in 30 minutes
Captures the scope decision (TV only), accessibility, light material, price targets and the 'not much to work with' reaction
Clear structure with verdict-style headers and timestamps
weaknesses: Only one action item; does not capture the individual-work expectation per role
Some repetition between summary and sections

evaluations.label: C
errors: 'Dolphin: freedom, smooth design': 'smooth design' is not supported ('Sure looks smooth' was said about the tiger drawing)
Action item 'Mark: Provide personal assignments to team members': the personal coach gives the assignments, not Mark
Names misspelled: 'Mark Knopp' (surname never given), 'Xavier Juukens', 'Dirk Mankveld'
Action items for Xavier ('Address material considerations') and UI designer ('Prepare intuitive design concepts') were not assigned in the meeting
Many timestamps do not match the transcript (e.g. scope clarified at 10:34, actually ~11:32)
strengths: Compact outline covering the main topics: brief, phases, whiteboard, animals, scope, accessibility, light material, pricing
Notes the limited margin from the price targets
weaknesses: Telegraphic fragments hard to understand for someone who missed the meeting
Action items are largely invented or misattributed
Misspelled names and an invented surname

evaluations.label: D
errors: 'Mark Knopf': surname never given in the transcript
Names misspelled: 'Dirk Mengveld' (Meinfeld), 'Xavier Jökens' (Juergens)
'UI designer also present (name not captured)': he introduced himself as Nick Broer
'rational changes only' is a doubtful reading of a garbled line ('No rational changes... revolutionary changes')
strengths: Clean, scannable structure a newcomer can act on
Correctly lists Xavier's three questions, the price targets, TV-only scope, accessibility, light material
Correctly states that personal assignments come via the personal coach and next meeting is in 30 minutes
weaknesses: No explicit action items section or owners
Omits that the marketing expert had no ideas ready yet and the 'not much to work with' reaction

rationale: B is the most accurate, with correct attributions, correct first names, the personal-coach detail and a clear next step; its errors are minor. D is concise and mostly correct but invents a surname, misses the UI designer's name and lacks owned action items. A is fairly complete but invents a project code, gets the PM's name wrong, misattributes the scope clarification and lists a settled question as open. C is fragmentary, adds unsupported details ('smooth design') and assigns action items that were never given, including attributing assignment distribution to Mark instead of the personal coach.
